verdict.rationale: RunAnywhere's own SDK docs show it running several model types on device: language models, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, vision-language models and image generation. That covers the LLM and multi-modal parts of the story. Nothing in the evidence supports the scale claim of hundreds of architectures, nor any mention of MoE or embedding models. Missing for 10: evidence of hundreds of supported architectures, MoE model support, embedding model support, a published model/architecture compatibility list, independent corroboration of breadth.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run hundreds of different model architectures including LLMs, MoE, multi-modal, and embedding models

citations.quote: The RunAnywhere Kotlin SDK runs language, speech, and vision models on the device.
`RunAnywhere.vlm` takes an image and a prompt.
`RunAnywhere.images` generates an image from a prompt.
`RunAnywhere.voice` assembles speech-to-text, a language model, and text-to-speech into one session that listens, thinks, and answers out loud.
